strengths: The paper identifies a useful distinction between pixel-level interventions and interventions on interpretable attributes, explaining why omitted attributes can confound feature–prediction associations. This has a clear audience in explainable AI and causal discovery.

PAGs and FCI provide an appropriate established framework for representing latent confounding and partial causal identification under the stated assumptions. Treating predictions as non-ancestors of image content is sensible background knowledge.

The causal-modeling background is generally accessible. The discussion usefully acknowledges limited identifiability, dependence on expert annotations, and difficulties with automatic feature construction.
The explicit synthetic data-generating process, two image applications, and detailed attribute mappings make the proposed workflow concrete.
weaknesses: Necessary: Preserve the distinction between possible and identified causes throughout the results. Section VI-C pools directed and circle–arrow edges into one bootstrap score, while subsequent text describes features as important or likely causes. A consistently recovered circle–arrow edge can still represent pure confounding, and bootstrap frequency is not a probability of causation. Furthermore, missing adjacency does not exclude an indirect causal effect. Report these statuses separately and narrow the conclusions accordingly.

Necessary: Address selection in the X-ray experiment. Controls are selected specifically for having 'no findings', so inclusion depends on the explanatory findings as well as pneumonia status. Conditioning on this selection can induce dependencies that undermine the causal interpretation used in the paper, which dismisses selection bias as irrelevant. Allowing latent confounding does not resolve this issue. Analyze the sampling mechanism or restrict this experiment to a descriptive illustration.

Necessary: Establish the reliability of the conditional-independence tests used for the empirical conclusions. With 239 X-rays and rare binary findings, or multicategory bird attributes conditioned on up to four variables, contingency tables can be sparse. The manuscript provides no cell-support diagnostics or sensitivity analysis establishing that the chi-square tests and resulting orientations are trustworthy. Bootstrap repetition does not correct systematic testing errors. Also clarify which data partition supplies the observations for FCI.

Necessary: Verify the simulation's claimed causal ground truth. Section V asserts that only H and V influence predictions, but the logistic coefficients are not reported, and the appendix specifies unpenalized regression, which does not enforce zero coefficients for C and T. Moreover, imperfect HydraNet detectors of H and V could respond to other shapes. Provide the actual decision rule and controlled shape-intervention checks, or enforce the claimed dependence by construction.

Necessary: Correct or clarify Example 1's Shapley derivation. On page 14, coalition expectations retain Z1's observational marginal when intervening on its parents Z2 or Z3; these are not generally the intervention quantities implied by the stated SCM. On page 15, the supposedly omitted Z3 remains fixed inside the calculation instead of being integrated through an observed-data estimator. Define the intervention-based coalition values consistently and rederive the comparison. A zero local attribution also does not establish global causal irrelevance.

Necessary: Reconcile the result descriptions and sample counts. Figure 8 and Section VI-C rank Size, Eye Color, and Bill Shape highest, whereas Figure 9 calls Wing Shape and Wing Pattern the most stable causes. Section VI-D dismisses Wing Color despite its higher plotted stability than either wing feature. If different edge types explain this discrepancy, show those results separately. The bird split counts sum to 3,898 rather than the reported 3,538, and 74.55% accuracy requires clarification for a stated 50-image X-ray test set.

Optional: A comparison with an associational method using the same macro-level annotations would help isolate the contribution of causal discovery from the benefit of supplying interpretable features. The qualitative LIME/SHAP examples primarily illustrate differences in explanatory representation.
